collection: Sealed · Volume I — Museum of Civil Liberties
note: The on-chain, declassifiable wing of Logos's Museum of Civil Liberties. Each piece seals an ENCRYPTED payload (an Internet Archive link + a short curatorial note on why the record belongs in the exhibition) behind a redaction. The linked document is public on the Archive; the payload — and which record a holder owns, and when they reveal it — is private, decrypted only with the owner's viewing key. 15 pieces across the Museum's five halls. All items officially declassified, public domain, or archived formerly-public pages — nothing active-classified.

pieces.title: Executive Order 6102 — Gold Confiscation
pieces.desc: By decree, holding your own gold became a crime. Proof that money you 'own' can be recalled by the state at will.

pieces.title: Nixon Closes the Gold Window
pieces.desc: The last tie between the dollar and gold, cut overnight. From here on, money is worth whatever power says it is.

pieces.title: Bank Secrecy Act — 'Patterns of Abuse'
pieces.desc: The law that conscripts your bank as an informant — every transaction watched, reported, and retained.

pieces.title: Church Committee Final Report
pieces.desc: The Senate's own record of intelligence agencies spying on, disrupting, and deceiving the citizens they served.

pieces.title: MKUltra Document 0000017748
pieces.desc: The CIA's experiments on unwitting people — surveillance and control turned inward, without consent.

pieces.title: CIA 'Family Jewels'
pieces.desc: The agency's private ledger of its own illegal acts: break-ins, wiretaps, and domestic spying it never meant to show.

pieces.title: Areopagitica
pieces.desc: Milton's case against licensing the press, printed in defiance of the censors it condemns — the founding argument for free expression.

pieces.title: Ulysses
pieces.desc: Banned as obscene for over a decade. What one era forbids, the next puts in the canon.

pieces.title: Lady Chatterley's Lover
pieces.desc: Suppressed for thirty years, until a jury asked whether the state should decide what adults may read.

pieces.title: The Pentagon Papers
pieces.desc: The secret history proving a public systematically lied to about a war — a people denied the truth they needed to consent.

pieces.title: COINTELPRO — The FBI's War on Dissent
pieces.desc: The FBI's covert program to 'expose, disrupt, and neutralize' dissent — the machinery of silencing, described in its own memos.

pieces.title: FBI Threat Letter to Dr. King
pieces.desc: An anonymous letter from the state urging a leader to take his own life. What power does to a voice it cannot tolerate.

pieces.title: SSCI CIA Torture Report — Executive Summary
pieces.desc: The Senate's declassified account of a torture program — control exercised beyond the law, then concealed.

pieces.title: Climate Change — US EPA
pieces.desc: A government science page, deleted at a change of power — the record rewritten in real time, surviving only because it was archived.

pieces.title: Climate Change — The White House
pieces.desc: Removed from the official site at the transition. The 'permanent record' lasts only as long as whoever controls the server allows.
